answer: Unrepeatable Answer Protocol. Each identity must answer a fresh, randomly generated constraint problem whose solution is a unique proof tied to that instance, like tracing one crevice across a glacier. Answers are checked for novelty against all prior submissions, so copying fails. A juniper-scented decoy pool seeds ambiguous instances to detect reuse. Every attempt costs a compute budget proportional to instance difficulty, and rejected duplicates still consume it. An attacker cloning identities must solve each instance independently, paying full compute per clone on that knoll of cost.
